facts.value: London Borough of Hackney Pension Fund — Treasury Management Strategy 2026-2029. Cover report to Pensions Committee, 30 March 2026 (doc 97651, 6 pp.), plus companion Appendix 1 (doc 97652, 5 pp., marked DRAFT). Cover paragraph 1.1 defines scope: the strategy 'proposes the Treasury Management Strategy for the Pension Fund for 2026-2029 for the operational cash balances that the Administering Authority maintains to manage daily transactions of the Fund. These transactions include the payment of pensions and transfers out together with the receipt of contributions from employers and payment of invoices. These balances are invested separately from the Council's own cash.' Appendix 1 p.2 reinforces: 'The strategy is broadly consistent to that agreed for 2023 - 2026 and is purely in relation to the management of cash, not the rest of the Fund's investments. From April 2026, this Treasury Management Strategy will only apply to cash held for the purpose of paying pensions in the short term (up to one year). Investment cash will be managed by the Pension Fund's investment pool, the London CIV.'

source.title: London Borough of Hackney Pension Fund — Treasury Management Strategy — Pensions Committee, 30 March 2026

facts.note: This is a Pension Fund paper, not a Council treasury paper. Read in full from local disk (cover 6 pp. + Appendix 1 5 pp.). Both documents held.

facts.value: Cover paragraph 4.4, verbatim: 'The Fund does not borrow; therefore, the strategy concerns only cash at bank and cash deposits. The Fund will maintain minimal cash balances to pay pensions and meet other obligations such as paying invoices and reimbursing the Council for Fund staff salaries and other recharges. The core position is 0 - 2.5% of Fund assets as agreed in the Investment Strategy Statement (ISS) and Strategic Asset Allocation.'

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — cover paragraph 4.4, page 2

facts.note: This is the sentence that makes the paper non-addressable by PWLBtoday. A Pension Fund carries no CFR, no external debt, no prudential indicators, no MRP. The Fund's investment side is out of scope of this strategy anyway (moving to London CIV from April 2026).

facts.value: Cover paragraph 4.13, table on page 4 — operational cash held in money market funds managed by the Council's Treasury Team at 28 February 2026: Invesco Sterling Liquidity Portfolio (Institutional) £4.250m; Fidelity Institutional Liquidity Sterling Fund (Class F) £4.526m; BlackRock Institutional Sterling Liquidity Fund (Heritage) £2.733m; Aberdeen Standard Liquidity Fund (Lux) - Sterling Fund (Class L1) £5.000m. Total £16.509m.

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — cover paragraph 4.13, page 4

facts.note: The Aberdeen holding at £5.000m sits at the £5m per-fund lending-list limit stated in Appendix 1. Four MMF providers with broadly even weightings.

facts.value: Cover paragraph 4.14, table on page 4 — Pension Fund bank account balances at 28 February 2026: LB of Hackney Pension Fund £1.032m; LB Hackney Pension Fund (LPPA) £16.442m. Total £17.474m. Cover paragraph 4.12: 'a new pension fund bank account was opened in September 2025 solely for the benefit activities of the newly appointed administrator LPPA'.

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — cover paragraphs 4.12 and 4.14, page 4

facts.note: Total operational cash disclosed in the paper = £16.509m (MMFs) + £17.474m (bank) = £33.983m at 28 February 2026. Paper does not itself sum the two tables. Custodian balance at Northern Trust is NOT disclosed in the paper — so this £33.983m is not the whole cash position of the Fund.

facts.value: Cover paragraph 4.15, table on page 5, and Appendix 1 page 5 — ISS approved by the Committee in November 2025, effective from 1 April 2026. Listed Equity 45.0% (range 45.0-50.0); Private Equity 0.00% (0.0-2.0); Private Credit 7.0% (4.0-10.0); Property/Real Estate 12.0% (10.0-14.0); Infrastructure 5.0% (3.0-7.0); Other Alternatives 9.0% (6.0-12.0); Credit 5.0% (3.0-7.0); UK Government Bonds 17.0% (14.0-20.0); Cash 1.0% (1.0-5.5), split Investment Cash 0.0% (0.0-3.0) and Operational Cash 1.0% (0.5-2.5). Footnote: 'Fund is responsible for managing operational cash at the Fund.'

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — cover paragraph 4.15, page 5; Appendix 1 page 5

facts.note: From 1 April 2026 the Fund's investment cash moves to London CIV; only operational cash remains under this strategy.

facts.value: Appendix 1 pp.3-4 — Fund uses the Council's lending list. Minimum long-term credit rating A- or equivalent for counterparties; AA+ or equivalent for non-UK sovereigns. Instruments: UK banks and building societies; DMADF; Business Reserve and Call Accounts; Variable-NAV Money Market Funds; UK Local Authorities; UK Central Government; UK Police and Fire Authorities; Corporate Institutions. 'Sufficient cash held on deposit either within the Pension Fund or at the Pension Fund administrators to cover one to two months' worth of benefit, transfer and invoice payments, with monies to be invested overnight or on short term deposits.' 'The lending list currently covers 6 funds with a limit of £5m each.'

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — Appendix 1 pages 3-4

facts.note: The 6-fund / £5m-per-fund lending-list ceiling means only £30m of MMF capacity is available under policy. Paper reports £16.509m held across 4 of those slots at 28 Feb 2026 — roughly half the ceiling used.

facts.value: Cover paragraphs 4.7-4.12 — Pension Fund cash held in three locations: (i) an in-house bank account for benefit payments and transfers, operated through outsourced administrator LPPA (Local Authority Pensions Partnership); (ii) a second bank account for fund-management payments (invoices, recharges to Council), managed by the Council's Treasury Team via deposits and Money Market Funds; (iii) cash with the Pension Fund custodian, Northern Trust, supporting fixed-income manager Columbia Threadneedle with derivative margin calls, capital calls and income distributions. From April 2026 (subject to 2026 LGPS regulations being in place), cash held with the custodian moves out of the Fund's internal team management and into London CIV.

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — cover paragraphs 4.7-4.12, pages 3-4

facts.note: The custodian balance is the third location and is not disclosed in this paper. From April 2026 it is no longer the Council's Treasury Team responsibility.

facts.value: Cover paragraph 4.5: 'The Council's 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy was approved by Council in March 2026.' Cover paragraph 4.6: 'The improved funding position resulting from the 2025 triennial valuation, combined with the reduction in employer contribution rates for most employers (including Hackney Council the largest employer), will reduce contribution income during the financial years 2026/27 to 2028/29.'

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — cover paragraphs 4.5 and 4.6, pages 2-3

facts.note: Paragraph 4.5 defers to the Council's own strategy for counterparty policy (Cabinet 2 March 2026 / Council 4 March 2026, appendix docs 96912 / 96978 held on disk but out of scope for this reading). Paragraph 4.6 is a Council cash-flow signal — reduced employer contribution income across 2026/27-2028/29 — relevant to a future read of the Council's own General Fund treasury book, not this Pension Fund paper.

facts.value: NOT APPLICABLE against this paper. Cover paragraph 4.4 states the Fund does not borrow. Our PWLB price book records 'HACKNEY LONDON BOROUGH COUNCIL' at 13 loans / £199,828,070 / 3.8677% weighted at 28 February 2026 (17 live loans at 15 August 2026: 1 under 12m, 2 at 1-2y, 2 at 2-5y, 6 at 5-10y, 6 at 10-25y) — but that borrower is the General Fund / HRA of the Council, not the Pension Fund. Any Council-level reconciliation belongs to a read of the Council's own Treasury Management Strategy (Council 4 March 2026, doc 96978) which is on disk but out of scope for this task.

source.title: OUR file — price_book.py 'HACKNEY LONDON BOROUGH COUNCIL' --as-at 2026-02-28

facts.note: The paper's own text puts the reconciliation out of scope. Recording the Council-level file for completeness so a future reader of the Council's own strategy has the figure ready. Not asserted, not used.

facts.value: NOT APPLICABLE. CFR - external borrowing - other long-term liabilities = internal borrowing is the Council identity; a Pension Fund does not have a CFR, holds no external borrowing and has no prudential indicators. The paper carries no such figures because they do not exist for the Fund.

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — verified absent

facts.note: Absence noted per RECORD_SCHEMA.md — a Pension Fund treasury strategy does not carry CFR / external borrowing / OLTL by design.

facts.value: Own arithmetic on the paper: MMFs (paragraph 4.13) £16.509m + bank accounts (paragraph 4.14) £17.474m = £33.983m total operational cash at 28 February 2026. Paper does not itself sum the two tables. Against Fund assets, 1.0% target operational-cash allocation from the ISS (paragraph 4.15) with a 0.5-2.5% tolerance range implies operational cash of roughly £24m at 1.0% or £60m at 2.5% on a £2.4bn fund (approximate Fund size — not stated in this paper). £33.983m sits comfortably inside the tolerance band on those assumptions.

source.title: Pension Fund Treasury Management Strategy — arithmetic on paragraphs 4.13, 4.14, 4.15

facts.note: Fund size is not printed in this paper. The £24m/£60m envelope is a directional sense-check only, not asserted.

summary.text:
Hackney Pension Fund's Treasury Management Strategy 2026-2029, heard at Pensions Committee on 30 March 2026. Cover report (doc 97651, 6 pp.) and Appendix 1 (doc 97652, 5 pp., marked DRAFT) both read in full from local disk. Report author Miriam Adams, Assistant Director Pension Investments and Administration; financial implications signed by Deidre Worrell, Director Financial Management, 19 March 2026.

This is a Pension Fund paper, not a Council treasury paper, and the distinction is dispositive for us. Cover paragraph 4.4 states plainly: 'The Fund does not borrow; therefore, the strategy concerns only cash at bank and cash deposits.' Appendix 1 page 2 narrows the scope further from April 2026: this strategy 'will only apply to cash held for the purpose of paying pensions in the short term (up to one year). Investment cash will be managed by the Pension Fund's investment pool, the London CIV.' A Pension Fund carries no CFR, no external debt, no prudential indicators and no MRP; the paper carries none of those figures because they do not exist for the Fund.

What the paper does carry: £33.983m of operational cash at 28 February 2026 — £16.509m across four Money Market Funds (Invesco £4.250m, Fidelity £4.526m, BlackRock £2.733m, Aberdeen Standard £5.000m at the £5m per-fund limit) plus £17.474m across two Pension Fund bank accounts (LB Hackney £1.032m and LB Hackney (LPPA) £16.442m). A third cash location — the Fund's custodian Northern Trust — is described but not sized; from April 2026 it moves under London CIV. The Investment Strategy Statement approved in November 2025 sets an operational-cash allocation of 1.0% (range 0.5-2.5%) of Fund assets; the paper does not print Fund size.

Loan-book reconciliation is not applicable. The PWLB price book records HACKNEY LONDON BOROUGH COUNCIL at 13 loans, £199.828m, 3.87% weighted at 28 February 2026 — but that entity is the Council's General Fund and HRA book, not the Pension Fund. A Council-level reconciliation belongs to a read of the Council's own Treasury Management Strategy (Council 4 March 2026, doc 96978), which sits on disk but is a separate paper. The balance-sheet identity is not applicable for the same reason. No draft.

Two observations recorded for a future Council-level read but not raised here. Cover paragraph 4.6 flags reduced employer contribution income across 2026/27-2028/29 following the 2025 triennial valuation — a Council cash-flow watch item, not a Fund item. And the report author and financial-implications officer are Pension Fund officers (Miriam Adams; Deidre Worrell), not the Council's S151. Naeem Ahmed is Group Director Finance & Corporate Resources for the Council and likely the S151, but this paper does not state that and it should be verified from the Council's own strategy before any Hackney contact.
